Looking at my situation — I'm in Quzhou, Hebei, on the North China Plain. My family has farmed here for generations. I know this land. What we do here is wheat and maize, same as everyone in the village. Same rotation my father used, same rotation my neighbors use. The local grain buyer is nearby, the seed shop sells what works here, and my land suits both crops.

I have about 10 mu. I'll plant all of it to winter wheat starting this October, then follow immediately with summer maize after the June harvest on the same ground. That's the full rotation — both seasons, same land. No cotton, no vegetables. I don't have the connections to sell those well, and the price risk is too high for me.

For wheat, I'll get the Jimai improved variety from the county seed station — it's reliable and my neighbor got good yield last year. I'll apply fertilizer at planting and top-dress at jointing. I need at least 3 irrigations: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I might do a fourth at grain filling if it's dry. Two or three pesticide sprays — one for aphids in spring, one fungicide around heading.

For maize, I'll use a hybrid — the ones from the agro-supply shop perform better than saving my own seed. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate once or twice if needed. Rotary tillage after wheat harvest to break up the stubble before planting.
